comparisons.visual_audit_method: All 64 recordings inspected at start, midpoint, scored end and final animation; three additional kill/death transition sequences inspected. Initial target references checked on flat and terraced terrain. Independent event/video checks passed for all 64 recordings; all 33 clear tails had no delayed death or kill discrepancy. This was sampled-frame review, not full playback of every video.

title: Zombie Protect evaluation
scope: Protect-only comparison. The original Hunt controller and recordings are unchanged.

methodology.control: Protect is an experimental SAM 2 supervisor calling ROCKET-2 Hunt, with tracking every five control steps and movement keys disabled. Knockback still moves the player. Protect means self-defense, not escorting another character.
methodology.input: The test script supplies initial SAM 2 points from the fixed scenario layout before gameplay. Actions after setup are generated by ROCKET-2 and the stated control filters. ROCKET-2 receives RGB, a visual target and previous actions; live health, position and kill statistics are used only for scoring.
methodology.scoring: Clear means all zombies killed while alive within 600 control steps. Kill/death counters are episode deltas. Auto-respawn is scored as death, with zero remaining health. Large unexplained position resets invalidate a trial.
methodology.repeats: Eight fresh placements/action seeds per situation in a separate Protect-only test selected after earlier Hunt/Protect tests. Earlier trials are not included in these totals. Hunt keeps the baseline controller. All trials use one fixed world; Minecraft entity AI randomness is not separately seeded. These results cover this benchmark only.
